summary: Rule recognises -webkit-line-clamp as a third tell (sibling declarations only, like the other two). Header comment rewritten: definition is hub-owned, recogniser set is repo-owned and grows here. notification-bell.scss's baseline entry removed (1 to 0); its 15 px-literal entries untouched. Site comment trimmed. Added a small node:test fixture, not wired into pnpm test/lint (both scoped elsewhere). pnpm lint passes, baseline one entry smaller (610 to 609 pre-existing).

acceptance.criterion: stylelint-rules/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden.mjs recognises -webkit-line-clamp on the same declaration block as a third tell, alongside text-overflow/white-space:nowrap and clip-path. It is an unusually safe tell: the declaration exists for no other purpose
acceptance.evidence: stylelint-rules/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden.mjs:120-123 adds `isLineClamped` reading `siblings.some((sib) => sib.prop.toLowerCase() === '-webkit-line-clamp')`, checked exactly like the existing `isTruncatingText`/`isVisuallyHidden` checks — sibling declarations only, never the selector/file/comment (siblingDecls() unchanged). Proven via the new fixture: `.row-snippet`-shaped CSS (`overflow: hidden; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical;`) produces 0 warnings (`node --test stylelint-rules/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden.test.mjs` → 'does not flag the multi-line clamp tell (-webkit-line-clamp) — T351' pass), and `pnpm lint`'s stylelint step against the live notification-bell.scss (which carries exactly that shape) reports 0 violations for this rule at that file (`stylelint: no new violations (609 pre-existing...)`, baseline no longer carries the entry — see next bullet).

acceptance.criterion: Its header comment is rewritten. It currently states that a third shape is a hub question and that the rule 'does not grow a third exemption locally'. That instruction is withdrawn — replace it with §4's refined split: the definition is hub-owned and moves only by amending ADR-0041; this tell list is local and grows here. State what still does escalate: a box that genuinely is a scrolling context and wants plain hidden anyway
acceptance.evidence: stylelint-rules/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden.mjs:11-57 (new header). Replaces the withdrawn sentence ('this rule does not grow a third exemption locally') with the definition/recogniser-set split verbatim in substance ('The definition above — what the rule is for. Hub-owned. It moves only by amending ADR-0041 §4' / 'The recogniser set below — ... Repo-owned, lives here, and is expected to grow ... adding one is not an ADR amendment and does not go to the hub'), and states the remaining escalation case ('What still comes to the hub: a box that genuinely IS a scrolling context a focus event could shift, and wants plain hidden anyway ... only an ADR-0041 amendment can move it'). Also updated the rule's rejected-message string (messages.rejected) to mention -webkit-line-clamp as a recognised sibling declaration, for consistency with the new tell — not requested verbatim by the acceptance text but a direct, in-scope consequence of teaching the rule a third tell (same message, one more clause).

acceptance.criterion: A regression check that the rule flags a genuine unpaired layout hidden and does not flag any of the three tells. There is no test file for this rule today — if adding one is more than a small fixture, say so in the report rather than growing the task
acceptance.evidence: New stylelint-rules/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden.test.mjs: 5 cases using Node's built-in test runner (node:test/node:assert, no new dependency) and stylelint's own programmatic `stylelint.lint({ code, config })` API against inline CSS fixtures — (1) flags a genuine unpaired `.shell { overflow: hidden; }`, (2) does not flag hidden paired with a following clip, (3) does not flag the text-overflow/white-space:nowrap tell, (4) does not flag the clip-path tell, (5) does not flag the -webkit-line-clamp tell. `node --test stylelint-rules/no-unpaired-overflow-hidden.test.mjs` → 'tests 5', 'pass 5', 'fail 0'. This turned out to be a small fixture (one file, ~90 lines, no new dependency, four inline snippets) so it was built rather than deferred — but it is NOT wired into `pnpm test` (`ng test`/`@angular/build:unit-test` is scoped to `src/**/*.spec.ts` per angular.json's `test.options.include`, and this rule intentionally lives outside `src/` as repo tooling, not application code) or into `pnpm lint` (`scripts/lint-all.mjs` runs `ng lint` and `scripts/stylelint-check.mjs` only, neither of which executes arbitrary test files). It is documented as a standalone command in the file's own header comment. Flagging this explicitly since wiring it into either pnpm script would be a change to files/behavior the task did not ask for.
